sections.label: Building the rules
paragraphs: With the new brand manual in hand, I established clear visual rules. Logo placement. Color specifications. Typography rules. Graphic elements and spacing systems. Every rule had to be flexible enough to work across print, digital, packaging, and merchandise.

sections.label: Consistent but flexible
paragraphs: The design system made the new brand consistent but not rigid. The core identity was strong enough that it would feel like Rokoko no matter where you encountered it.

sections.label: Presentation templates
paragraphs: I built Google Slides templates so teams could make decks that felt branded without a designer. That took hours off presentation prep.

sections.label: Social media system
paragraphs: Social media branding covered Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, and YouTube with templates and guidelines. Everything from grid posts to job listings to YouTube thumbnails carried the same visual language.

sections.label: Email templates
paragraphs: Email templates prioritized clarity and personality. Marketing could update them without rebuilding the layout. The tone was always friendly but professional.

sections.label: Packaging
paragraphs: Packaging for the first hardware product under the new brand was minimal and bold. Unboxing felt premium and deliberate, in line with Rokoko's position in the market.

sections.label: Consistency by default
paragraphs: After the rebrand, Rokoko had one visual language across every platform. The team could make new assets without checking every decision. Consistency became the default.

sections.label: Market perception
paragraphs: The unified brand system changed how Rokoko read in the market. They felt more polished and more trustworthy: a company making innovative products, not one still experimenting with the technology.
